# Leaf

> Leaf is a free, open-source ebook reader for macOS that aims at the reading experience of a Kindle: tunable typography, time left in the chapter and the book, find in book, with highlights and notes planned. It opens EPUB, MOBI and AZW3 files directly from Finder without a library or account, remembers where you stopped reading, and quits when you close the window. Requires macOS 15 or later. MIT License. Independent project, not affiliated with Amazon.

Leaf is built with SwiftUI and WebKit and uses foliate-js to parse and paginate books. It deliberately has no bookshelf, library, store or sync: you double-click a file, read, and close the window. MOBI and AZW3 files must be DRM-free; books bought from the Kindle Store usually carry DRM and cannot be opened.

## Key facts

- Formats: EPUB, MOBI, AZW3 (DRM-free)
- Platform: macOS 15 or later; universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs
- Price: free; source code under the MIT License
- Download: about 2.7 MB DMG
- Reading position: remembered per book, identified by file content (survives renaming or moving)
- Progress: click the bottom-right corner to cycle percent, location, time left in chapter, time left in book; estimates learn from your own page turns
- Contents: floating panel (⌘T or click the chapter name), highlights the current chapter, closes on selection
- Find in book: ⌘F, results listed by chapter with matches highlighted on the page; ⌘L jumps to a percent or location
- Typography: any installed font or original / sans / serif, size 80–200%, five weight levels, line / paragraph / letter spacing, margins, text width, one or two columns, justified or left; built-in presets Compact / Standard / Large / Low Vision plus custom presets
- Themes: paper, sepia, dark or follow the system
- Interface languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish
- Not included by design: store, account, sync, library, PDF
- First launch: Leaf is not notarized by Apple; allow it once in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway

## How it compares

- Apple Books: built into macOS and opens EPUB and PDF, but does not import MOBI or AZW3, and adds books to its library.
- Calibre: opens MOBI, AZW3 and EPUB and is centered on library management (about 350 MB download, macOS 14+, GPL-3.0); its viewer can also be launched on its own.
- Leaf: opens all three formats without a library, in a 2.7 MB app, with Kindle-style progress, typography presets and find in book.
